Billet aluminum engine covers
What does your pilot or repeat batch need?

Examples cover pilot lots and mixed components, including short-run housings. Orders start at 1 piece. Share the geometry, material, finish and inspection requirements so we can quote the batch plan and price.

Geometry & process
For pilot builds, mixed-part orders and smaller repeat batches. Milling, turning, multi-axis machining and casting finishing can support different part numbers within a production program.
Size & workholding
Share models, overall dimensions and stock sizes for each part number. Dedicated fixtures and revision control support repeatable setups across batches. Identify common features and parts that must fit together so tool access and clamping space can be reviewed.
Material & finish
Specify the grade, material condition and finish for each part number. Identify cosmetic criteria and required final dimensions for batch acceptance.

Drawing & acceptance
Drawing requirements

Provide a part list with revision, quantity and material for each item. Identify common features and any parts that must fit or be supplied together.

Distinguish an initial approval batch from later releases. Identify which requirements remain fixed and how proposed drawing changes should be reviewed.

Inspection and acceptance

Specify first-article reporting, subsequent sampling and traceability requirements with the quotation request.

Agree treatment of cosmetic criteria, mixed revisions and nonconforming parts before defining batch acceptance.

Agree the measurement method and required records before production.

7–14 business days — Production, from 1 piece. Production starts after drawing and order confirmation. The period includes surface finishing; shipping time is additional.

Equipment and order records
Prepare your low-volume production enquiry

Share quantities per part and release, required documentation, finish and packaging needs.

Give expected repeat demand as a forecast and requested dates for confirmation. Agree commercial terms separately.

Prepare RFQ email

Add your requirements to the email draft, then attach drawings in your email app before sending.
